📖 SOP — How DWM Performance is Calculated

1. Equivalent Units (EU) — the common yardstick

Each SA Type has a reference material (the Equivalent Material, configured under Capacity → Capacity Plan). The total std hours per piece of that material defines "1 EU" — the baseline unit of work for that SA. Different materials with different complexity all get normalized to this baseline so they can be summed and compared.

Example: if the reference material has std hrs = 8 hrs/piece, then producing 1 piece worth 16 std hrs = 2 EU.

2. Planned EU (the green solid line + KPI)

Daily Planned EU (per SA) = (Manpower × Shift Hrs × Shifts × Eff%/100) ÷ Equiv Std Hrs
Period Planned EU = Sum of daily Planned EU across all days in the period

Where Manpower, Shift Hrs, Shifts, and Efficiency% come from your Capacity Plan for each SA, and Equiv Std Hrs is the std hrs/piece of that SA's reference material.

3. Capacity @ Attendance EU (the dashed blue line)

Same formula as Planned EU, but Manpower is replaced with attendance-pro-rated headcount:

Pro-rated MP = Present Total × (SA Planned MP ÷ Total Planned MP)
Present Total = sum of attendance statuses for the day (Present=1.0, Overtime=1.0, Half-Day=0.5, Absent=0)

Fallback: if no attendance is logged for a particular date, Cap @ Attendance EU = Planned EU for that date (the dashed line sits exactly on the green line — visible only once attendance starts getting logged).

4. Earned Hours

The value of work produced, measured in standard hours.

Earned Hours (per entry) = Quantity Completed × Std Hrs per Piece
(stored as stdHrs when the entry is saved)
Period Earned Hours = Sum of stdHrs from all entries in the period

Earned Hours rewards output, not time spent at station. This is the SAP/Oracle standard and the "P" in OEE (Performance = Earned ÷ Run Hours).

5. Actual EU (orange bars + KPI)

Actual EU = Sum of (each SA's Earned Hours ÷ that SA's Equiv Std Hrs)

Each SA gets normalized to its own EU baseline before summing, so mixing materials of different complexity is mathematically correct.

6. Productivity %

Productivity % = Earned Hours ÷ Actual Hours × 100

Industry-standard labor productivity. Above 100% means faster than standard; below 100% means slower.

  • ≥ 85% — On track (green)
  • 70 – 85% — Needs attention (amber)
  • < 70% — Action required (red)

7. Plan Adherence %

Plan Adherence % = Actual EU ÷ Planned EU × 100

Did we produce what we planned to? Same colour bands as Productivity.

8. Lost Hours & Lost Units (EU)

Lost Hours = Sum of delayHrs from entries in the period
Shortfall EU = max(0, Planned EU − Actual EU) · Lost EU = Delay Hrs ÷ Equiv Std Hrs

Lost Hours come directly from delay entries (PF, MS, QH, CW, etc.). Shortfall EU = production gap to plan (Planned − Actual). Lost EU = delay hours converted to EU — production lost specifically due to delays.

9. Operator Performance

For each operator within the period, productivity is computed as Earned Hrs ÷ Actual Hrs × 100, sorted high to low. Same green/amber/red colour bands. The chart helps identify top performers and operators who may need support.

10. Data Sources Summary

Capacity Plan (Capacity tab) → Manpower, Shift Hrs, Shifts, Days, Efficiency, Equivalent Material
Entries (Entries tab) → Actual Hrs, Std Hrs (= Earned Hrs), Delay Hrs, Qty Completed, Operator
Work Orders → Material → SA Type linkage (for attribution)
Materials master → Std Hrs per piece (for EU conversion)
Attendance (Attendance tab) → Present / Absent / Half-Day status (for Cap @ Attendance line)
💡 Tip: Productivity tells you how efficient your team is at standard. Plan Adherence tells you how much you delivered against plan. You can have 130% productivity but 60% plan adherence (working fast but understaffed) — both metrics together give the full picture.

⬆ Import PPC Dispatch Plan

Paste rows copied directly from Excel (tab-separated), or upload an .xlsx file. Expected columns, in order:
Source · Machine No · Token no. · TK (ignored — auto-derived as Source-Token) · Type · M/c Dispatch Month (YYYY-MM or Jun-26) · SA Type · SA Number · Material No · Auto SA Target (ignored — auto-calculated) · Man SA Target · Kit complete (Yes/No) · All Kit Completed Date
Rows sharing the same Machine No are grouped into one machine. Rows with a blank Machine No are grouped in runs of 3 (WKH/WLH/TS-style) — a new machine starts whenever an SA Type repeats. Source and Token apply once per machine (first non-blank value found in its group is used). "Kit complete = Yes" with no date fills in today's date.
